metadata.title: Pegylated Liposomal Doxorubicin 20 mg/m² – 21 day
metadata.indication: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma with CD4 <200 cells/mm³ and extensive mucocutaneous or visceral disease.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Organ-function values or categories are optional; omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source-reconciled organ-function encoding · clinical/pharmacy review pending

organ_function_reconciliation.note: Structured renal/hepatic component rules were reconciled to the current official NCCP regimen source. Independent Consultant and oncology-pharmacy validation remains pending.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.

source_evidence.limitation: Original PDF bytes were unavailable and screenshot tool responses did not contain inspectable table pixels. All ambiguous printed boundaries remain review-only.

metadata.draft_scope: External batch 3 clinical draft; application not changed; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending.
audit_limitations: Current audit uses complete extracted official text; original PDF bytes and visual table inspection are unverified.
Prior discontinuation and dose-reduction history must survive current toxicity recovery; a missing history value is not a confirmed absence.
Every numerical modified dose remains a Consultant/pharmacy prescription decision; no automatic calculation from an unknown original/current dose.
NCCP 00462 infusion timing differs from current EMA AIDS-KS instructions; local oncology/pharmacy reconciliation is required.
The standard calendar is 21 days; the source allows a separately selected 14 day alternative, not two concurrent phases.
NCCP 00462 count rules must not inherit 00205 recovery or growth-factor choices.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: All dose changes require Consultant discussion and pharmacy verification of original/current prescription, prior toxicity and concurrent modifications. This tool does not authorise treatment.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00462 Version 4. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.
clinical_governance.organ_function_rule_status: Current extracted text reconciled in external batch 3 draft; visual table review and independent Consultant/pharmacy validation remain pending.

indications.description: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma with CD4 <200 cells/mm³ and extensive mucocutaneous or visceral disease.

treatment.schedule_summary: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² IV on day 1 every 21 days, maximum 6 cycles. A 14 day interval is a separately selected Consultant option for some patients.
treatment.duration: Maximum 6 cycles, or earlier progression or unacceptable toxicity

alternative_cycle_intervals.note: NCCP p1: a 14 day cycle may be more appropriate in some patients; not concurrent with the 21 day calendar.

hypersensitivity.label: Hypersensitivity to PLD, peanut, soya or excipients

options.label: Source grade 2

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.label: Worst relevant non-haematological toxicity

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild or asymptomatic; observation only and intervention generally not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; minimal, local or non-invasive intervention may be indicated; may limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospital care may be indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the exact adverse event and grade it using its own CTCAE criteria, objective findings, intervention required and functional impact.

eligibility: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma with CD4 <200 cells/mm³ and extensive mucocutaneous or visceral disease (NCCP p1).
exclusions: Hypersensitivity to pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or excipients (NCCP p1); EMA SmPC 4.3 specifically includes peanut/soya.
EMA SmPC 4.3: not for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma effectively treatable with local therapy or systemic alfa-interferon. This is a product-specific restriction, distinct from NCCP eligibility.
Do not substitute Myocet/non-pegylated or conventional doxorubicin for the pegylated liposomal formulation.
monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile, LDH, ECG and ECHO/MUGA LVEF (NCCP p2).
Before each cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile; ECG monitoring. LDH, ECHO/MUGA and PPE assessment as clinically indicated (NCCP p2).
LVEF assessment is mandatory before each additional administration exceeding lifetime cumulative anthracycline 450 mg/m²; this is not an automatic treatment stop (NCCP p4).
Response assessment follows the Consultant plan. No universal CT interval or LDH threshold is specified. Review HIV treatment and opportunistic-infection care with the treating service.
dose_modifications: NCCP Table 1: ANC ≥1 AND platelets ≥75 allow 100% from this domain. ANC 0.5–0.99 OR platelets 50–74 select the 50% row; ANC <0.5 OR platelets <50 delay. Fractional gaps (ANC >0.99 to <1; platelets >74 to <75) require interpretation.

NCCP Table 2: renal/haemodialysis adjustment is not expected; bilirubin 20–50 µmol/L selects 75% of original dose; 51–86 selects 50% of original; >86 not recommended. The gap >50 to <51 is not interpolated.

NCCP Table 3: PPE/stomatitis decisions depend jointly on current grade, prior grade 3–4 toxicity and 0/1/2 weeks delay. Grade 3–4 at two weeks leads to discontinuation; a later recovered grade must not erase that decision. Original/current dose and concurrent reasons require Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation; no automatic restart dose.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Risk assigned from the most emetogenic active component and treatment phase.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
additional_supportive_care: Low emetogenic potential; follow current NCCP/local antiemetic policy.
PPE prevention for 4–7 days after treatment: cool hands/feet, avoid excessive heat/hot water and tight gloves, socks or shoes, following local advice.
Anaphylaxis facilities are required. Prior reaction infusion changes require supervision and resolution of the active reaction.
Coordinate HIV/antiretroviral and opportunistic-infection care with the treating team; this regimen does not specify universal primary G-CSF or antimicrobial prophylaxis.
supportive_care.premedication: None usually required (NCCP p4); individualise after an infusion reaction.

treatment_phases.label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma
treatment_phases.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin

administration.notes: NCCP: first infusion 1 mg/min; later 60 minutes only if no reaction. Glucose 5% 250 mL, or 500 mL for total dose ≥90 mg; no in-line filter. Prior reaction pathway requires supervision: 5% over 15 min, double rate next 15 min if tolerated, remainder over 1 hour. Current EMA AIDS-KS section describes 30 min: reconcile this NCCP/SmPC difference locally before administration. A selected 14 day cycle is an alternative schedule; it does not add doses to this 21 day calendar.

treatment_phases.schedule_summary: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² IV on day 1 every 21 days, maximum 6 cycles. A 14 day interval is a separately selected Consultant option for some patients.
